--- ## Walkthrough Changed bind-address/network selection to prefer IPv6 wildcard binding for multi-CIDR and dual-stack cases: when multiple cluster/service CIDRs exist the code now selects `"[::]:6443"` with `bindNetwork = "tcp"`. Tests and render command expectations were updated to reflect this dual-stack binding behavior. ## Changes |Cohort / File(s)|Summary| |---|---| |**Operator network observation**
`pkg/operator/configobservation/network/observe_network.go`|Updated service bind selection: multi-CIDR/dual-stack now sets `bindAddress = "[::]:6443"` and `bindNetwork = "tcp"` (broadened IPv6/dual-stack condition).| |**Operator network tests**
`pkg/operator/configobservation/network/observe_network_test.go`|Added dual-stack scenarios and assertions: verifies `servicesSubnet` ordering and that dual-stack cases set `servingInfo.bindAddress` to `"[::]:6443"` and `servingInfo.bindNetwork` to `"tcp"`.| |**Render command behavior**
`pkg/cmd/render/render.go`|Changed bind-address/network selection to use number of `ClusterCIDR` entries: multi-CIDR => `"[::]:6443"` and `BindNetwork = "tcp"`; single-CIDR keeps prior per-CIDR parsing for IPv6 vs IPv4.| |**Render command tests**
`pkg/cmd/render/render_test.go`|Updated dual-stack expected values: `cfg.ServingInfo.BindAddress` changed to `"[::]:6443"` and `cfg.ServingInfo.BindNetwork` to `"tcp"`.| ## Estimated code review effort 🎯 3 (Moderate) | ⏱️ ~25 minutes
✨ Finishing Touches
🧪 Generate unit tests (beta) - [ ] Create PR with unit tests

Tests result showed :point_down: 
- This change preserves the ipv6 single-stack behaviour (see [payload job](https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/prow-artifact-archive/logs/openshift-cluster-kube-apiserver-operator-2079-nightly-4.22-e2e-metal-ipi-ovn-ipv6/2036705559805169664))
- This change helps the dual-stack install to complete as expected (see [ipv6-primary dual-stack](https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/prow-artifact-archive/logs/multi-pr-openshift-installer-10380-openshift-cloud-provider-aws-135-openshift-cluster-ingress-operator-1376-openshift-cluster-kube-apiserver-operator-2079-e2e-aws-ovn-dualstack-ipv6-primary-techpreview/2036704654946996224) and [ipv4-primary dual-stack](https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/prow-artifact-archive/logs/multi-pr-openshift-installer-10380-openshift-cloud-provider-aws-135-openshift-cluster-ingress-operator-1376-openshift-cluster-kube-apiserver-operator-2079-e2e-aws-ovn-dualstack-ipv4-primary-techpreview/2036704670189096960))

I suppose it makes sense to open both IPv4 and IPv6 socket when running on dual-stack :eyes: This brings it closer to how openshift-apiserver is set up (see [here](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-openshift-apiserver-operator/blob/af62d47f901e3739bb049cd3914c073551df7958/bindata/v3.11.0/config/defaultconfig.yaml#L25-L26) that also sets `tcp` as the bindNetwork).
